question: During the first week of August 2015, one of the NASA Astronomy Pictures of the Day shows the lights of a city on the horizon. The namesake of this city also has a landmark building in Chicago named after him. What is the name of the architectural firm that designed this landmark building? Give the first name appearing in the name of the firm as of June 2023.

history.name: Astronomy_Picture_Analysis_Expert

- Identify the APOD entry (Aug 1–7, 2015) that explicitly mentions city lights on the horizon.
- Determine the city and the person it’s named after.
- Find the Chicago landmark named after that person.
- Determine the architectural firm and its official name as of June 2023, then extract the first name in the firm’s name.
I will start by scanning APOD entries for Aug 1–7, 2015 and highlight any mention of city lights on the horizon.

history.name: InformationVerification_Expert

The textual description indicates the city lights of Marquette, Michigan glow along the horizon across the lake. This appears to match the criterion.
Candidate: Aug 6, 2015 — description mentions city lights of Marquette visible on the horizon over Lake Superior.

history.name: InformationVerification_Expert

City identified: Marquette (Michigan). I’ll proceed to namesake linkage.

history.name: ArchitecturalHistory_Expert
history.content:
Namesake connection: The city of Marquette (Michigan) is named after Father Jacques Marquette (17th-century French Jesuit missionary and explorer). In Chicago, there is a landmark building named after him: the Marquette Building (140 S. Dearborn Street), a Chicago Landmark.
Architectural firm: The Marquette Building was designed by Holabird & Roche (1893–1895). The successor firm’s name as of June 2023 is Holabird & Root. The first name in the firm’s name is “Holabird.”
